parsed.explanation: Visitor-facing exposure is low: foreign markers including 'X' accepted with no extra gender scrutiny, no presentation offence, accommodation discrimination prohibited, bathroom access protected, and documented social acceptance (91% rights support), plus active city safer-spaces and police reporting infrastructure. Offsetting negatives: rising report volumes (trans reports up 51%, only six convictions), threat-framed hostility at Pride events, and a documented custody gap — no rule governs placement, municipal-record designation and case-by-case factors apply, trans detainees are often held on an Extra Care wing with sex offenders, and drafted guidelines remain unpublished. That is a real state-imposed exposure, but it is conditional on detention rather than universal, and courts have treated gender-mismatched wings as aggravating imprisonment, showing partial working recourse. No border, facility or care exclusion is documented, so the rating sits in reduced risk, below the fully-documented acceptance tier.
